source: /data/use-of-english/ (the Master page's own items, so a mistake on the Board and on the page is one mistake)

rounds.prompt: She is very good ___ solving puzzles.
rounds.note: Good at + -ing.

rounds.prompt: I am looking forward ___ seeing you next week.
rounds.note: Look forward to + -ing.

rounds.prompt: He apologised ___ being late.
rounds.note: Apologise for.

rounds.prompt: Many students depend ___ their parents for money.
rounds.note: Depend on.

rounds.prompt: The teacher was proud ___ her class.
rounds.note: Proud of.

rounds.prompt: We were surprised ___ the news.
rounds.note: Surprised at or by.

rounds.prompt: There is no point ___ arguing about it.
rounds.note: No point in + -ing.

rounds.prompt: She is interested ___ learning Japanese.
rounds.note: Interested in.

rounds.prompt: What is the reason ___ this delay?
rounds.note: Reason for.

rounds.prompt: ___ it was raining, we went for a walk.
rounds.note: Although + a full clause.

rounds.prompt: We went out ___ the bad weather.
rounds.note: Despite + a noun phrase. Although needs a clause.

rounds.prompt: I will call you as soon ___ I arrive.
rounds.note: As soon as.

rounds.prompt: He studied hard in ___ to pass.
rounds.note: In order to.

rounds.prompt: She did not go out ___ she had finished her homework.
rounds.note: Until gives the time when something changes.

rounds.prompt: He is rich; ___, he is not happy.
rounds.note: However links two ideas and takes a comma.

rounds.prompt: We will be late ___ we leave now.
rounds.note: Unless means if not.

rounds.prompt: I wish I ___ more time to study.
rounds.note: Wish + past tense for a present regret.

rounds.prompt: He was made ___ stay after school.
rounds.note: Passive of make takes a to-infinitive.

rounds.prompt: You ___ better see a doctor about that cough.
rounds.note: Had better + bare infinitive.

rounds.prompt: Not only ___ she win the race, but she also broke the record.
rounds.note: Inversion after not only needs an auxiliary.

rounds.prompt: The window ___ broken last night.
rounds.note: Passive, past simple.

rounds.prompt: He asked me ___ I could help him.
rounds.note: Reported yes/no question.

rounds.prompt: The girl ___ sits next to me is my cousin.
rounds.note: Who for people as the subject.

rounds.prompt: That is the man ___ car was stolen.
rounds.note: Whose shows possession.

rounds.prompt: This is the house ___ I grew up.
rounds.note: Where for places.

rounds.prompt: She told me about her trip, ___ sounded amazing.
rounds.note: Which refers back to the whole idea.

rounds.prompt: I will never forget the day ___ we met.
rounds.note: When for times.

rounds.prompt: There is not ___ milk left in the fridge.
rounds.note: Any in negatives. Milk is uncountable.

rounds.prompt: I have ___ friends in this city, so I feel lonely.
rounds.note: Few + countable nouns, with a negative feeling.

rounds.prompt: How ___ time do we have left?
rounds.note: Much with uncountable nouns.

rounds.prompt: I tried both options, but ___ of them worked.
rounds.note: Neither is for two things. Watch the spelling: neither.

rounds.prompt: ___ of my friends lives near me; they all live far away.
rounds.note: None is for more than two.

rounds.prompt: She is old ___ to drive.
rounds.note: Enough comes after the adjective. Watch the spelling: enough.

rounds.prompt: At first I did not like him, but I got used ___ his jokes.
rounds.note: Get used to + noun or -ing.

rounds.prompt: I would rather stay home ___ go out tonight.
rounds.note: Would rather ... than. Not then.

rounds.prompt: As far ___ I know, the shop closes at six.
rounds.note: As far as I know.

rounds.prompt: She has been working here ___ 2019.
rounds.note: Since + a point in time.

rounds.prompt: He did it on ___ because he wanted to annoy me.
rounds.note: On purpose.

rounds.prompt: I cannot find my keys. Can you help me look ___ them?
rounds.note: Look for means search.

rounds.prompt: The meeting was called ___ because the manager was ill.
rounds.note: Call off means cancel.

rounds.prompt: She grew ___ in a small village.
rounds.note: Grow up.

rounds.prompt: We ran ___ of milk, so I went to the shop.
rounds.note: Run out of.

rounds.prompt: By the time we arrived, the film ___ already started.
rounds.note: Past perfect: an action finished before another past action.

rounds.prompt: The new bridge has ___ built to reduce traffic in the town centre.
rounds.note: Present perfect passive: has been + past participle.

rounds.prompt: The results will ___ announced on Friday.
rounds.note: Future passive: will be + past participle.

rounds.prompt: She hates ___ laughed at.
rounds.note: Passive gerund: being + past participle, after verbs like hate, like and avoid.

rounds.prompt: I ___ not realise how late it was until I looked at the clock.
rounds.note: Past simple negative: did + not + base verb.

rounds.prompt: She enjoys swimming, and so ___ her brother.
rounds.note: So + auxiliary + subject. The auxiliary matches the first verb: enjoys, so does.

rounds.prompt: Our teacher ___ to be a professional dancer before she started teaching.
rounds.note: Used to describes past states. Would cannot be used for states like be.

rounds.prompt: It ___ have been Tom who phoned; he is abroad this week.
rounds.note: Cannot have + past participle: you are sure it was impossible.

rounds.prompt: I should ___ listened to your advice.
rounds.note: Should have + past participle: a past regret or mistake.

rounds.prompt: Yesterday we ___ to wait an hour for a table.
rounds.note: The past of have to is had to. Must has no past form.

rounds.prompt: All the players ___ been asked to bring a passport, so please check yours.
rounds.note: Present perfect passive with a plural subject: have been asked.

rounds.prompt: By this time next year, I ___ have lived here for ten years.
rounds.note: Future perfect: will have + past participle.

rounds.prompt: Little ___ she know that the exam had been cancelled.
rounds.note: Negative adverbials such as little, never and hardly are followed by inversion with an auxiliary.

rounds.prompt: Nobody showed Tom how to play the guitar, so he taught ___.
rounds.note: Reflexive pronoun: the subject and the object are the same person.

rounds.prompt: We really enjoyed ___ at the party.
rounds.note: Enjoy + reflexive pronoun. Watch the plural: ourselves.

rounds.prompt: The two friends have known each ___ for years.
rounds.note: Each other: a reciprocal pronoun.

rounds.prompt: ___ was raining so heavily that we stayed indoors.
rounds.note: It is the subject for weather, time and distance.

rounds.prompt: ___ used to be a cinema on this street.
rounds.note: There + be introduces something that exists or existed.

rounds.prompt: My phone fell in the sea, so I had to buy a new ___.
rounds.note: One replaces a countable noun when it is a different thing. It would mean the same phone.

rounds.prompt: The museum, ___ opened in 1998, attracts thousands of visitors every year.
rounds.note: After a comma (non-defining clause) use which, not that.

rounds.prompt: The woman to ___ I spoke was very helpful.
rounds.note: Preposition + whom for people.

rounds.prompt: I could not understand ___ he was saying.
rounds.note: What means the thing that.

rounds.prompt: I felt so ill that I did not eat ___ all day.
rounds.note: Anything in negative sentences. Nothing would make a double negative.

rounds.prompt: Many students prefer working in groups because it helps ___ to learn from each other.
rounds.note: Object pronoun after helps.

rounds.prompt: The city is famous for ___ ancient walls.
rounds.note: Its, with no apostrophe, is the possessive of it.

rounds.prompt: We visited four countries in two weeks, and ___ one was very different.
rounds.note: Each or every + one, for the items in a group taken separately.

rounds.prompt: We have not finished yet, so we need ___ ten minutes.
rounds.note: Another + number + plural noun means that many more.

rounds.prompt: Some people prefer cities, while ___ prefer the countryside.
rounds.note: Others means other people. No noun follows.

rounds.prompt: I have two brothers, and ___ of them are doctors, like me.
rounds.note: Both of + plural pronoun, for two people.

rounds.prompt: I spent the ___ weekend revising for the exam.
rounds.note: The whole + singular noun. All would not follow the.

rounds.prompt: It rained ___ day yesterday, so we stayed in.
rounds.note: All day means from morning to night.

rounds.prompt: Who is ___ best player in your team?
rounds.note: The before a superlative.

rounds.prompt: Hardly ___ people came to the concert, so it was cancelled.
rounds.note: Hardly any means almost none.

rounds.prompt: There is not ___ point in complaining about it now.
rounds.note: Not much or not any with uncountable nouns.

rounds.prompt: I have ___ few friends who live nearby, so I see them quite often.
rounds.note: A few is positive (some). Few alone is negative (hardly any).

rounds.prompt: ___ four years, the Olympic Games take place in a different country.
rounds.note: Every + number + plural noun for regular intervals.

rounds.prompt: I have ___ idea what he is talking about.
rounds.note: No idea. Not and none cannot go directly before a noun.

rounds.prompt: I wonder ___ the shop is open on Sundays.
rounds.note: If or whether introduces an indirect yes/no question.

rounds.prompt: She looked at me as ___ nothing had happened.
rounds.note: As though or as if + past perfect for an unreal comparison.

rounds.prompt: She speaks French and German, as ___ as English.
rounds.note: As well as means and also.

rounds.prompt: Some people love big cities, ___ others prefer village life.
rounds.note: While or whereas shows a contrast between two groups.

rounds.prompt: She spoke slowly ___ that everyone could understand.
rounds.note: So that + clause shows purpose.

rounds.prompt: Take an umbrella in ___ it rains.
rounds.note: In case + clause: as a precaution.

rounds.prompt: You can borrow my car as ___ as you drive carefully.
rounds.note: As long as means on condition that.

rounds.prompt: Hurry up, ___ you will miss the bus.
rounds.note: Otherwise means if you do not.

rounds.prompt: I did not go to the party. ___, I stayed at home and read a book.
rounds.note: Instead means in place of the thing just mentioned.

rounds.prompt: I will not change my mind, even ___ you ask me again.
rounds.note: Even if + a possible future situation.

rounds.prompt: I cannot decide ___ to accept the job or not.
rounds.note: Whether + to-infinitive. If cannot be used here.

rounds.prompt: ___ hard I try, I cannot open this jar.
rounds.note: However + adjective or adverb means no matter how.

rounds.prompt: It was not ___ I got home that I realised I had lost my wallet.
rounds.note: Not until marks the point when something first happened.

rounds.prompt: He was ___ tired that he fell asleep at his desk.
rounds.note: So + adjective + that + result.

rounds.prompt: It was ___ a beautiful day that we decided to have a picnic.
rounds.note: Such + a + adjective + noun + that + result.

rounds.prompt: I was ___ surprised to say anything.
rounds.note: Too + adjective + to-infinitive means more than is needed to do it.

rounds.prompt: The film was far better ___ I expected.
rounds.note: Comparative + than. Watch the spelling: than, not then.

rounds.prompt: She is not as tall ___ her sister.
rounds.note: Not as + adjective + as.

rounds.prompt: The harder you work, ___ better your results will be.
rounds.note: The + comparative, the + comparative.

rounds.prompt: The longer the journey, the ___ tired we became.
rounds.note: The + comparative, the + comparative. Tired takes more.

rounds.prompt: This is by far the ___ difficult exam I have ever taken.
rounds.note: Superlative of a long adjective: the most + adjective.

rounds.prompt: The new model is ___ more expensive than the old one.
rounds.note: Much, far, even or still can strengthen a comparative. Very cannot.

rounds.prompt: No sooner had we sat down ___ the waiter brought the menu.
rounds.note: No sooner ... than. Hardly ... when is the matching pair.

rounds.prompt: I try to eat ___ sugar than I used to.
rounds.note: Less with uncountable nouns. Fewer is for countable nouns.

rounds.prompt: There were so ___ people at the concert that we could not move.
rounds.note: So many + countable noun + that + result.

rounds.prompt: Many people are afraid ___ flying.
rounds.note: Afraid of.

rounds.prompt: We enjoyed the trip in spite ___ the rain.
rounds.note: In spite of + noun phrase.

rounds.prompt: The match was cancelled because ___ the weather.
rounds.note: Because of + noun phrase. Because alone needs a clause.

rounds.prompt: Why not walk instead ___ taking the bus?
rounds.note: Instead of + noun or -ing.

rounds.prompt: She has been famous ___ her cooking since she won a TV competition.
rounds.note: Famous for.

rounds.prompt: I have not seen her ___ three weeks.
rounds.note: For + a length of time.

rounds.prompt: This design is similar ___ the one we used last year.
rounds.note: Similar to.

rounds.prompt: In addition ___ English, she speaks Italian and Greek.
rounds.note: In addition to + noun or -ing.

rounds.prompt: We were introduced ___ each other at the party.
rounds.note: Introduce someone to someone.

rounds.prompt: I am not familiar ___ this software.
rounds.note: Familiar with.

rounds.prompt: The book was written ___ a famous Spanish author.
rounds.note: By + the agent in a passive sentence.

rounds.prompt: Heavy rain prevented us ___ leaving the house.
rounds.note: Prevent someone from + -ing.

rounds.prompt: ___ to the forecast, it will snow tomorrow.
rounds.note: According to + a source of information.

rounds.prompt: ___ from Maria, everybody passed the test.
rounds.note: Apart from means except for.

rounds.prompt: I am worried ___ my exam results.
rounds.note: Worried about.

rounds.prompt: She specialises ___ marine biology.
rounds.note: Specialise in.

rounds.prompt: Over two hundred runners took ___ in the charity race.
rounds.note: Take part in means participate.

rounds.prompt: We set ___ at dawn to avoid the traffic.
rounds.note: Set off or set out means begin a journey.

rounds.prompt: Scientists carried ___ a series of experiments on the new drug.
rounds.note: Carry out means do and complete a task.

rounds.prompt: The weather turned ___ to be much better than the forecast.
rounds.note: Turn out to be describes a surprising result.

rounds.prompt: She decided to give ___ smoking last year.
rounds.note: Give up means stop doing something.

rounds.prompt: I came ___ my old diary while I was tidying the attic.
rounds.note: Come across means find by chance.

rounds.prompt: Can you find ___ what time the train leaves?
rounds.note: Find out means discover information.

rounds.prompt: If you keep spending money like that, you will end ___ broke.
rounds.note: End up + adjective means finally be in a situation.

rounds.prompt: The manager promised to deal ___ the complaint immediately.
rounds.note: Deal with means take action about.

rounds.prompt: I get ___ very well with my new colleagues.
rounds.note: Get on or get along means have a good relationship.

rounds.prompt: Nothing can make ___ for the time we have lost.
rounds.note: Make up for means compensate for.

rounds.prompt: I cannot put up ___ this noise any longer.
rounds.note: Put up with means tolerate.

rounds.prompt: On the other ___, the journey was cheaper than expected.
rounds.note: On the one hand ... on the other hand.

rounds.prompt: In the ___, we decided to stay at home.
rounds.note: In the end means finally.

rounds.prompt: At ___, we did not understand the rules, but later it became clear.
rounds.note: At first contrasts with later.

rounds.prompt: As a ___, many shops had to close.
rounds.note: As a result introduces a consequence.

rounds.prompt: It was a difficult choice, but ___ the whole I think we chose well.
rounds.note: On the whole means in general.

rounds.prompt: By the ___, did you remember to buy the tickets?
rounds.note: By the way adds a new or less important topic.

rounds.prompt: I cannot come. I have too much work and, ___ any case, I do not feel well.
rounds.note: In any case means whatever happens.

rounds.prompt: You can stay with us for the time ___.
rounds.note: For the time being means for now, but not permanently.

rounds.prompt: The doctor will see you soon. In the ___, please take a seat.
rounds.note: In the meantime means while waiting.

rounds.prompt: Some animals, for ___, sleep standing up.
rounds.note: For example or for instance introduces an illustration.

rounds.prompt: I broke the vase by ___; I did not mean to.
rounds.note: By accident is the opposite of on purpose.

rounds.prompt: The wedding will take ___ in a small church.
rounds.note: Events take place. People take part.

rounds.prompt: Please make ___ that you lock the door when you leave.
rounds.note: Make sure or make certain.

rounds.prompt: Students must pay ___ to the teacher during lessons.
rounds.note: Pay attention to.

rounds.prompt: It was lovely to meet you. Let us keep in ___.
rounds.note: Keep in touch means stay in contact.

rounds.prompt: You should take ___ of the good weather and go for a walk.
rounds.note: Take advantage of.

rounds.prompt: She has made great ___ in her English this year.
rounds.note: Make progress. Watch the spelling: progress.

rounds.prompt: Social media plays a major ___ in how young people communicate.
rounds.note: Play a part or play a role.

rounds.prompt: He caught ___ of a rare bird as he walked through the forest.
rounds.note: Catch sight of means see suddenly.

rounds.prompt: It is important to do your ___ to protect the environment.
rounds.note: Do your best, or do your bit.

rounds.prompt: The company went out of ___ after thirty years.
rounds.note: Go out of business means stop trading.

rounds.prompt: He suggested ___ to the beach for the day.
rounds.note: Suggest + -ing.

rounds.prompt: She admitted ___ the window.
rounds.note: Admit + -ing.

rounds.prompt: She is said ___ be the richest woman in Europe.
rounds.note: Passive reporting: is said to + infinitive.

rounds.prompt: My parents want me ___ become a doctor.
rounds.note: Want someone to + infinitive.

rounds.prompt: He told me ___ he would call me the next day.
rounds.note: Reported statement: told someone that + clause.

rounds.prompt: She ___ me that she was moving to Canada.
rounds.note: Tell is followed by a person. Say is not.

rounds.prompt: He spoke quietly so ___ not to wake the baby.
rounds.note: So as (not) to + infinitive shows purpose.

rounds.prompt: I look forward to ___ from you soon.
rounds.note: Look forward to + -ing, because to is a preposition here.

rounds.prompt: I prefer tea ___ coffee.
rounds.note: Prefer one thing to another.

rounds.prompt: He insisted ___ paying for the meal.
rounds.note: Insist on + -ing.
